newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian communists win governorship in Stavropol.
newsitem.headline: Russian communists win governorship in Stavropol.

text.p: Russia's communist opposition won the governorship of the southern Stavropol region in a regional election at the weekend, official results showed on Monday.

Communist candidate Alexander Chernogorov won 55 percent of the vote in a runoff against Kremlin-appointed Pyotr Marchenko, who got just over 40 percent. The remaining votes were cast against both candidates.

In a first round of voting in the important south Siberian region of Altai, communist-backed candidate Alexander Surikov was in the lead with more than 46 percent of votes, with current governor Lev Korshunov with more than 43 percent.
In Murmansk in the far north incumbent governor Yevgeny Komarov was leading with 32 percent, far ahead of his rivals. Runoffs will be held in both regions on December 1.
In Kamchatka region in the far east, current governor Vladimir Biryukov led with some 48 percent and officials said a second round was likely to be held on December 8.
Voting also took place in three autonomous ethnic areas.

Heads of autonomous areas, like the more important regions and ethnic republics, all sit in Russia's upper chamber of parliament, the Federation Council, giving them a voice in national legislation and other questions of state.
In the Komi-Permyatsk area, part of Tyumen region in western Siberia, incumbent governor Nikolai Poluyanov was re-elected.
In the Koryak autonomous area, part of the Kamchatka region, the governorship was won by a woman lawyer Valentina Bronievich.
And in the Ust-Ordynsk Buryat autonomous area, part of Irkutsk region in central Siberia, voters elected Valery Maleyev, the director of a state farm.
